answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut and the incumbent has explicitly refused to reopen price this cycle, closing off negotiate_terms and making renewal (c1, c6) unlikely to meet the cost target. The contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, so defer_decision risks an unplanned lapse—unlike the earlier deferral in c5, which was for a non-critical service with slack, not a primary line feeding an assembly process at 94% committed volume with no buffer. Switching primary vendor (supported by c2's low-cost, quick-onboarding history) best serves the TCO objective, but that record is a year old and onboarding risk against a zero-buffer line is real, so I want the archived c2 record verified before committing capital, plus c4 to confirm negotiation truly has no remaining leverage. Given the tight timeline and no slack in the line, I'm scoping this as a small guarded test (partial volume shift) rather than a full cutover, preserving the option to fall back to the incumbent or add a second source next cycle if the new vendor underperforms.
